deployment.cacheContract: two policies, one module (DECISIONS/0029 P2): code and app metadata answer `cache-control: no-cache` with a content `ETag` and reply `304` to a matching `If-None-Match`; model weights, the recognition dictionary and the runtime WASM keep `no-store` and advertise no validator, because the worker's Cache API owns them and a second copy in the HTTP cache would be dead weight and a staleness path. Warm liveness is proven by *no body served over the origin* for anything the caches hold — and after ticket 17c a `304` is evidence for that claim rather than a violation of it.
deployment.contentEncoding: identity — nothing is compressed, so wire bytes equal file bytes
deployment.threads: Latency measured at 1 ORT thread (serve-app.mjs sends no COOP/COEP; the harness's 4-thread measurement is superseded). If isolation headers are added, latency improves and the footprint table regenerates.
deployment.remeasureRequiredAfter: discharged here: DECISIONS/0012 F11 trigger 1 (the PWA exists) was this ticket, and this measurement is the discharge

deployment.warmStructuralRequestsNote: Each of these is structural, not a cache miss: a service worker cannot intercept the fetch of its own script or that script's imports, and W6's version probe deliberately bypasses the cache. An unexplained warm request fails the run, so this list is exhaustive by construction.

cold.description: first visit, empty context and empty caches, fresh server instance

warm.description: same context, page.reload() — DECISIONS/0012 F8's revalidation clause is replaced by 'answered by the active caches' (DECISIONS/0027 W15), because this origin answers no 304

repeat.description: supplementary — a second inference in the same page with both sessions warm, driven by the app's own Re-run OCR

measurement.byteCounting: summed from the origin's own request log (scripts/serve-measure-app.mjs), which sees the worker's install precache, the WASM and the model downloads that page resource timings do not; HTTP header bytes are excluded
measurement.timingAnchor: performance.timeOrigin of the measured document. appReadyMs is the navigation's load event; firstResultMs is the instant a page-side poll observed the inference finish (busy-state gone) with the draft rendered. No Playwright round-trip is inside either number.
measurement.centralValue: median, with min and max published beside it. With n=5 no percentile is claimed (DECISIONS/0012 F2).
measurement.latencyBases: cold and warm are timed from their own navigation. The repeat phase has no navigation, so its firstResultMs is the duration from handover to result. appReadyMs is published for cold and warm only.

image.note: re-derivable from this script rather than from a gitignored dataset snapshot: the receipt is drawn on a canvas exactly as playwright/capture.spec.ts draws it, so the declared image is committed code. It is user data either way and never a network request. This supersedes the harness run's benchmarks/datasets/raw/sroie/assets/ex.jpg, which needs the 2.7 GB raw snapshot to re-derive — a published number nobody else can reproduce is not a measured one.

crossCheck.rule: DECISIONS/0028 T3: two drivers count the same bytes at the same origin, so they must agree exactly. Neither artifact may be rewritten to match the other.

findings.detail: Chromium HTTP cache retains ~6-8 MiB per entity; the 14.85 MB ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm answers 200 with full body on every warm visit, while 7 of 8 assets revalidate as 304
findings.evidence: session probe: 6 MiB entity retained, 8 MiB entity not retained, same server/headers as harness; 512 MB disk cache rules out eviction
findings.remedy: ticket 17 Cache API; header changes cannot fix browser per-entity limits
findings.affectsClaim: section 9 initial-download / re-fetch cost, not the local-processing claim (same-origin only)
findings.resolution: the worker precaches the runtime WASM into the Cache API, which is not subject to the HTTP cache's per-entity limit; this artifact's warm visit no longer lists it (DECISIONS/0027 W16)

findings.detail: a warm visit moves 2700 B over the wire, and the requests that reached the origin are /assets/models/manifest.json, /sw.js, /assets/cache-names-BCswqTtv.js
findings.evidence: this artifact's warm runs[]: five samples per class, counted from the origin's own request log (DECISIONS/0012 F5), cross-checked at ±0 against benchmarks/results/warm-bytes.json
findings.affectsClaim: section 9 initial-download / re-fetch cost: the second visit is no longer priced at the runtime WASM

history.why: the origin began answering code assets with an ETag, so a warm visit revalidates instead of re-downloading

findings.detail: the worker's module chunk no longer moves a body on a warm visit; it answers revalidated-304 at 0 B
findings.evidence: the warm runs[] path list and per-path status in this artifact, against benchmarks/results/warm-bytes.json's warmPerAsset
findings.remedy: ticket 17c: an ETag on code assets, which DECISIONS/0012 F10 measured already revalidating correctly under the entity limit. the ETag change and the regeneration of both footprint artifacts land in the same commit (DECISIONS/0028 T3/T7): a header change moves the number two artifacts publish
findings.affectsClaim: the warm-visit byte total, not the local-processing claim

findings.detail: the browser's /sw.js byte-check now sends If-None-Match and is answered with a 304 carrying no body, so the worker script costs 0 B on a warm visit
findings.evidence: the warm runs[] entry for /sw.js in this artifact: its status, bodyBytes and etag
findings.affectsClaim: which of the three warm line items the ETag actually removed

totals.cacheHeldBasis: deterministic: the built worker's precache manifest (packages/pwa/dist/app/sw.js, stat'd from disk) plus the verified model set named by assets/models/manifest.json. Not 'bytes currently in the named caches', which would depend on eviction (DECISIONS/0028 T8, DECISIONS/0027 W18).
totals.pageObservationNote: The page's own resource timings cover only the resources the *document* fetched. The worker's install precache, the WASM and the model downloads are not document resources and never appear here — that is why F5 counts bytes at the origin. So this pair is reported beside the totals and never added to them, and it is not the header cost of the whole visit.

provenance.table: packages/core/README.md, between the footprint markers, generated by benchmarks/scripts/render-footprint-table.mjs
provenance.supersedes: the harness measurement archived at benchmarks/results/footprint-2026-11-04-16ae8de.json (21,299,089 B cold / 14,848,852 B warm at 4 ORT threads). Also the withdrawn "~4.3 MB complete OCR pipeline" claim (ADR-002), which stays withdrawn.

sequencing.why: ticket 18 writes claims against the generated table, and while that table is the harness's it would be citing harness bytes as product bytes — the exact failure ADR-002 and DECISIONS/0012 F1 exist to prevent. The ETag header change is post-SW honest measurement's remaining known cost and belongs to 17c, which changes what ships, not what is measured.

provenance.note: measuredAt and the request log are the record of one run on one machine. Latency is not a constant: it is a distribution of n samples on the declared class, and a different machine class will produce a different table.
